newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Zaire's Mobutu expected to go to France in June.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu expected to go to France in June.

text.p: Zaire's ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko, given asylum in Morocco for "humanitarian reasons", is expected to leave for France at the beginning of June, a senior Moroccan official said on Saturday.

"President Mobutu, who was welcomed by Morocco for humanitarian reasons, is expected to leave for France as his final destination at the beginning of June unless there are complications in his health," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Mobutu, 66, and members of his family arrived on Friday in Morocco and are staying in the heavily guarded Amphitrite Hotel at the seaside next to the royal palace at Skhirat, 20 kms (12 miles) south of Rabat.

Quoting a government statement, the official news agency MAP said: "President Mobutu has asked permission to spend a few days in Morocco for health reasons before going to his permanent place of residence."
Mobutu owns a mansion on the French Riviera near Monte Carlo where he convalesced after being treated for prostate cancer earlier this year.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Friday that France would consider a request for asylum but had not received one.
"France has received no request from Marshal Mobutu," Juppe told France-Info radio. "We would look into it," he added when asked what he would do if he received such a request.

A Rabat-based Western diplomat said Mobutu would leave Morocco after the parliamentary election in France, "to avoid embarrassing French President Jacques Chirac's supporters". The first round of the election is on Sunday and the second a week later, on June 1.
